title: Operations with Decimals
seo_title: Grade 6 Multiplying and Dividing Decimals Worksheets (TEKS 6.3E, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.3E multiply and divide positive rational numbers fluently
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 decimal worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.3E: add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals, divide by a decimal, and multi-step word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: To divide by a decimal, move both decimal points the same number of places.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Add and subtract: line up the decimal points. Write zeros to fill empty places.
  • Multiply: multiply as whole numbers, then count the decimal places in both factors.
  • Divide by a whole number: put the decimal point straight up into the quotient.
  • Divide by a decimal: move the decimal point in both numbers the same number of places to make the divisor a whole number.

Examples

Example

4.56 ÷ 0.12

Move both points 2 places

456 ÷ 12

Answer: 38

Example

2.35 × 1.4

235 × 14 = 3,290

3 decimal places

Answer: 3.29

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digitsLine up the decimal points.
Counting decimal places wronglyAdd the decimal places of both factors.
Moving the decimal point in only the divisorMove it the same number of places in both numbers.

faq.a: Multiply and divide positive rational numbers fluently.

faq.q: Why move the decimal point in both numbers?
faq.a: It multiplies both by the same power of 10, so the quotient does not change.

faq.q: How do I check a decimal answer?
Do I need zeros at the end?
faq.a: Write zeros to fill places when adding or dividing. They do not change the value.

items.q: Add. The gray zeros hold the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 3.6 as 3.600 so every place has a digit. 12.405 + 3.600 = 16.005.

items.q: Subtract. The gray zeros hold the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 45.6 as 45.60 so every place has a digit. 45.60 − 7.83 = 37.77. Check: 37.77 + 7.83 = 45.6.

items.q: Add. The gray zeros hold the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8.07 as 8.070 so every place has a digit. 8.070 + 15.968 = 24.038.

items.q: Subtract. The gray zeros hold the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 30 as 30.000 so every place has a digit. 30.000 − 4.256 = 25.744. Check: 25.744 + 4.256 = 30.

items.q: Caleb lined up the last digits and got 7.63. What is the correct sum of 6.25 + 13.8?
items.e: Caleb lined up the last digits, so the 8 tenths were added to the 5 hundredths. Line up the decimal points instead and write 13.8 as 13.80: 6.25 + 13.80 = 20.05. Estimate: 6 + 14 = 20.

items.q: To find 6.3 − 2.875, how should you write 6.3?
items.e: 2.875 has 3 decimal places, so give 6.3 three places too. Zeros at the end do not change the value: 6.3 = 6.300. (6.003 puts the zeros in front of the 3, which changes 3 tenths into 3 thousandths.)

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 48.92 + 31.075?
items.e: Round to whole numbers: 48.92 ≈ 49 and 31.075 ≈ 31. 49 + 31 = 80. (About 52 comes from lining up the last digits.) The exact sum is 79.995.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 2.75 = 10.1
items.e: Find the missing addend by subtracting: 10.1 − 2.75. Write 10.1 as 10.10: 10.10 − 2.75 = 7.35. Check: 7.35 + 2.75 = 10.10 = 10.1. (12.85 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers: 235 × 14 = 3,290. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 3.290 = 3.29.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers: 308 × 25 = 7,700. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 7.700 = 7.7.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers: 126 × 45 = 5,670. Count the decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 5.670 = 5.67.
Multiply as whole numbers: 2,175 × 36 = 78,300. Count the decimal places: 2 + 2 = 4. Count 4 places from the right: 7.8300 = 7.83.
Multiply as whole numbers: 438 × 25 = 10,950. Count the decimal places: 3 + 1 = 4. Count 4 places from the right: 1.0950 = 1.095.
Multiply as whole numbers: 6 × 3 = 18. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.018.
Multiply as whole numbers: 47 × 8 = 376. Count the decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.376.
Multiply as whole numbers: 125 × 36 = 4,500. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 4.500 = 4.5.
Multiply as whole numbers: 45 × 2 = 90. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.090 = 0.09.
Multiply as whole numbers: 156 × 25 = 3,900. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2. Count 2 places from the right: 39.00 = 39.
Multiply as whole numbers: 705 × 4 = 2,820. Count the decimal places: 2 + 2 = 4. Count 4 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.2820 = 0.282.
Multiply as whole numbers: 314 × 25 = 7,850. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 7.850 = 7.85.

Multiply as whole numbers: 625 × 16 = 10,000. Count the decimal places: 2 + 2 = 4. Count 4 places from the right: 1.0000 = 1.

items.q: Without multiplying, how many decimal places does 3.125 × 0.04 have before you drop any zeros?
items.e: 3.125 has 3 decimal places and 0.04 has 2. The product has 3 + 2 = 5 places: 3,125 × 4 = 12,500, so 3.125 × 0.04 = 0.12500 = 0.125.

items.q: Which product is less than 5.2?
items.e: Compare the other factor with 1. Only 0.98 is less than 1, so only 5.2 × 0.98 is less than 5.2 (it is 5.096). 5.2 × 1 is exactly 5.2.

items.q: Which is the product of 19.8 × 3.05? Use an estimate.
items.e: Estimate: 19.8 ≈ 20 and 3.05 ≈ 3, so the product is about 20 × 3 = 60. Only 60.39 is close to 60. (22.85 is the sum.)
1 + 1 = 2 decimal places: count 2 places from the right in 510 → 5.10. The zero at the end can be dropped: 5.1. Count the places before you drop the zero, or you get 0.51.

sets.title: Divide a decimal by a whole number

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. 18.72 ÷ 6 = 3.12. Check: 3.12 × 6 = 18.72.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. 0.936 ÷ 4 = 0.234. Check: 0.234 × 4 = 0.936.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. 25.38 ÷ 9 = 2.82. Check: 2.82 × 9 = 25.38.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. 41.65 ÷ 7 = 5.95. Check: 5.95 × 7 = 41.65.

items.q: The quotient digits are written, but the point is missing. What is 9.144 ÷ 3?
items.e: Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. When 3 does not fit, write 0 in the quotient. 9.144 ÷ 3 = 3.048. Check: 3.048 × 3 = 9.144.

items.q: The quotient digits are written, but the point is missing. What is 2.385 ÷ 5?
items.e: Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. 2.385 ÷ 5 = 0.477. Check: 0.477 × 5 = 2.385.

items.q: The quotient digits are written, but the point is missing. What is 63.6 ÷ 12?
items.e: Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. 63.6 ÷ 12 = 5.3. Check: 5.3 × 12 = 63.6.

Divide as with whole numbers. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend. When digits run out, write zeros (7.5 = 7.500) and keep dividing until nothing is left. 7.5 ÷ 4 = 1.875. Check: 1.875 × 4 = 7.5.

items.q: Diego is dividing 7.5 ÷ 4. He has written 1.8 in the quotient, and 3 tenths are left. What should he do next?
items.e: 7.5 = 7.50 = 7.500, so writing zeros does not change the dividend. Write a 0 and keep dividing: 30 hundredths ÷ 4 = 7, 2 left; 20 thousandths ÷ 4 = 5. So 7.5 ÷ 4 = 1.875. (1.83 writes the remainder as a digit.)

items.q: Which multiplication checks that 18.72 ÷ 6 = 3.12?
items.e: Quotient × divisor = dividend. 3.12 × 6 = 18.72, so the division is right.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 4.56 ÷ 0.12?
items.e: 0.12 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right). 4.56 ÷ 0.12 = 456 ÷ 12 = 38. Check: 38 × 0.12 = 4.56.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 1.5 ÷ 0.25?
items.e: 0.25 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right) and write a zero in 1.5. 1.5 ÷ 0.25 = 150 ÷ 25 = 6. Check: 6 × 0.25 = 1.5.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 2.24 ÷ 0.7?
items.e: 0.7 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 2.24 ÷ 0.7 = 22.4 ÷ 7 = 3.2. Check: 3.2 × 0.7 = 2.24.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 0.63 ÷ 0.009?
items.e: 0.009 has 3 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 1,000 (move both points 3 places right) and write a zero in 0.63. 0.63 ÷ 0.009 = 630 ÷ 9 = 70. Check: 70 × 0.009 = 0.63.

items.q: Which problem has the same quotient as 7.35 ÷ 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10: 7.35 → 73.5 and 0.5 → 5. 7.35 ÷ 0.5 = 73.5 ÷ 5 = 14.7. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.

items.q: Which problem has the same quotient as 0.18 ÷ 0.006?
items.e: 0.006 has 3 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 1,000: 0.18 → 180 and 0.006 → 6. 0.18 ÷ 0.006 = 180 ÷ 6 = 30. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.

items.q: Which problem has the same quotient as 12 ÷ 0.75?
items.e: 0.75 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100: 12 → 1,200 and 0.75 → 75. 12 ÷ 0.75 = 1,200 ÷ 75 = 16. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.
0.8 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 9.6 ÷ 0.8 = 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Check: 12 × 0.8 = 9.6.
0.12 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right). 0.144 ÷ 0.12 = 14.4 ÷ 12 = 1.2. Check: 1.2 × 0.12 = 0.144.
1.5 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 3.75 ÷ 1.5 = 37.5 ÷ 15 = 2.5. Check: 2.5 × 1.5 = 3.75.
0.45 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right) and write zeros in 27. 27 ÷ 0.45 = 2,700 ÷ 45 = 60. Check: 60 × 0.45 = 27.
0.3 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 0.51 ÷ 0.3 = 5.1 ÷ 3 = 1.7. Check: 1.7 × 0.3 = 0.51.
0.13 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right) and write a zero in 6.5. 6.5 ÷ 0.13 = 650 ÷ 13 = 50. Check: 50 × 0.13 = 6.5.
2.4 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 14.4 ÷ 2.4 = 144 ÷ 24 = 6. Check: 6 × 2.4 = 14.4.
0.07 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right). 0.0084 ÷ 0.07 = 0.84 ÷ 7 = 0.12. Check: 0.12 × 0.07 = 0.0084.
0.9 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 52.2 ÷ 0.9 = 522 ÷ 9 = 58. Check: 58 × 0.9 = 52.2.
0.016 has 3 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 1,000 (move both points 3 places right) and write zeros in 7.2. 7.2 ÷ 0.016 = 7,200 ÷ 16 = 450. Check: 450 × 0.016 = 7.2.

items.q: Without dividing, which is true about 8 ÷ 0.4?
items.e: 0.4 is less than 1, and many 0.4s fit into 8, so the quotient is greater than 8. 8 ÷ 0.4 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20. (2 is 8 ÷ 4, and 3.2 is 8 × 0.4.)

items.q: Ethan wrote 4.85 ÷ 0.5 = 0.97. What mistake did he make?
c: Moved the point only in the divisor
Moved the point in both numbers
items.e: Ethan changed 0.5 to 5 but left 4.85 as it was: 4.85 ÷ 5 = 0.97. He moved the point only in the divisor. Move both: 4.85 ÷ 0.5 = 48.5 ÷ 5 = 9.7.

items.q: Why does 4.56 ÷ 0.12 have the same answer as 456 ÷ 12?
c: Only the divisor was multiplied by 100
items.e: 4.56 × 100 = 456 and 0.12 × 100 = 12. When both numbers are multiplied by 100, the quotient does not change, just as 6 ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 20 = 3. Both give 38.

items.q: Gas costs $3.48 per gallon. Mia buys 12.5 gallons. How much does she pay?
A 2.5-pound bag of apples costs $4.35. What is the price per pound?
items.e: Price per pound = cost ÷ pounds = 4.35 ÷ 2.5. Move both points 1 place: 43.5 ÷ 25 = 1.74. Check: 2.5 × $1.74 = $4.35. ($1.85 subtracts, and $6.85 adds.)

items.q: Aaliyah has 6.75 m of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces 0.45 m long. How many pieces does she get?
Four friends eat dinner. The bill is $86.40 and they add a $13.60 tip. They split the total equally. How much does each friend pay?
One lap of a track is 0.4 km. Sofia runs 7.5 laps. How far does she run?
items.e: Multiply: 7.5 × 0.4. 75 × 4 = 300, and 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places give 3.00 = 3 km. (7.9 km is the sum.)

items.q: Gabriel runs 5 km in 27.5 minutes at a steady pace. How many minutes does each kilometer take?
items.e: Divide: 27.5 ÷ 5. 275 ÷ 5 = 55, and the point goes above the point: 5.5 minutes. Check: 5 × 5.5 = 27.5. (22.5 subtracts.)

items.q: A car goes 31.5 miles on 1 gallon of gas. How far can it go on 8.4 gallons?
items.e: Multiply: 31.5 × 8.4. 315 × 84 = 26,460, and 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places give 264.60 = 264.6 miles. Estimate: 30 × 8 = 240.

items.q: A truck drove 283.5 miles and used 13.5 gallons of gas. How many miles did it go per gallon?
items.e: Miles per gallon = miles ÷ gallons = 283.5 ÷ 13.5. Move both points 1 place: 2,835 ÷ 135 = 21. Check: 21 × 13.5 = 283.5. (270 subtracts.)

items.q: Ethan buys 3 notebooks for $2.85 each and a pen for $1.49. He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get?
One batch of granola needs 0.75 cup of honey. Grace makes 2.5 batches. How much honey does she need?
items.e: Multiply: 2.5 × 0.75. 25 × 75 = 1,875, and 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places give 1.875 cups. (3.25 is the sum.)

items.q: Store A sells 12 oz of cereal for $3.48. Store B sells 18 oz for $4.86. Which is the better buy per ounce?
items.e: Unit price = cost ÷ ounces. A: $3.48 ÷ 12 = $0.29 per ounce. B: $4.86 ÷ 18 = $0.27 per ounce. $0.29 − $0.27 = $0.02, so Store B is cheaper by $0.02 per ounce. ($1.38 compares the box prices.)

items.q: Fabric costs $6.40 per yard. Mateo needs 2.75 yards for a costume. How much does the fabric cost?
items.e: Multiply: 2.75 × $6.40. 275 × 64 = 17,600, and 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places give 17.600 = $17.60. Estimate: 3 × $6 = $18. ($9.15 is the sum.)

items.q: Three friends share a pizza order that costs $47.25. They split it equally. How much does each friend pay?
items.e: Divide: $47.25 ÷ 3. 4,725 ÷ 3 = 1,575, and the point goes above the point: $15.75. Check: 3 × $15.75 = $47.25. ($141.75 multiplies, and $44.25 subtracts.)

items.q: Each lap of the pool takes Josiah 1.25 minutes. He swims for 15 minutes. How many laps does he swim?
items.e: Divide: 15 ÷ 1.25. Move both points 2 places: 1,500 ÷ 125 = 12. Check: 12 × 1.25 = 15. (18.75 multiplies.)

items.q: A tank holds 37.8 L of water. How many 0.6 L bottles can be filled from it?
Isabella wants to bike 30 km this week. She rides 12.6 km on Monday and 8.75 km on Tuesday. How many more kilometers does she need to ride?
items.e: Step 1: 12.60 + 8.75 = 21.35 km so far. Step 2: 30.00 − 21.35 = 8.65 km. (21.35 km is the distance already ridden. 19.99 km comes from lining up the last digits.)

items.q: A pack of 8 pencils costs $3.60. A pack of 12 pencils costs $4.80. How much less does one pencil cost in the 12-pack?
items.e: 8-pack: $3.60 ÷ 8 = $0.45 per pencil. 12-pack: $4.80 ÷ 12 = $0.40 per pencil. $0.45 − $0.40 = $0.05. ($1.20 compares the pack prices.)

items.q: Diego runs 0.25 mile in 2.4 minutes. At the same pace, how long does it take him to run 3 miles?
items.e: Step 1: 3 ÷ 0.25 = 300 ÷ 25 = 12 quarter miles. Step 2: 12 × 2.4 = 28.8 minutes. (7.2 minutes multiplies 3 × 2.4, as if the 2.4 minutes were for a whole mile.)

items.q: A car uses 0.04 gallon of gas per mile. Gas costs $3.50 per gallon. How much does the gas cost for a 185-mile trip?
items.e: Step 1: 185 × 0.04 = 7.4 gallons. Step 2: 7.4 × $3.50 = $25.90. ($7.40 stops after step 1: that is gallons, not dollars.)

items.q: Luis has 4.8 m of fabric. Each costume needs 0.75 m. How many costumes can he make, and how much fabric is left?
items.e: 4.8 ÷ 0.75 = 480 ÷ 75 = 6.4, so only 6 whole costumes fit. They use 6 × 0.75 = 4.5 m, and 4.8 − 4.5 = 0.3 m is left. (0.4 m reads the .4 of 6.4 as meters, but 0.4 of a costume is 0.4 × 0.75 = 0.3 m.)
